newsitem.title: UK: ICI to build 12 mln stg paint plant in India.
newsitem.headline: ICI to build 12 mln stg paint plant in India.

text.p: British paints and chemicals company ICI Plc said on Tuesday that it would construct a new 12 million stg paints plant in the northern Indian town of Chandigarh.
The facility which would have an annual capacity of 20 million litres is expected to be ready by Spring 1998, ICI said in a statement.
"It will produce paint for the decorative and automative refinish markets initially in the local domestic market, but with an eye on potential exports from India in the future," ICI said.
ICI earlier had plants in the eastern city of Calcutta and in the southern city of Hyderabad.
The group has recently spent 7.5 million stg to set up another plant in Thane, on the outskirts of the western city of Bombay which has capacity of 20 million litres a year.
"With the commissioning of the Mumbai (Bombay) plant, ICI Paints India will have production capacity of 50 million litres a year," ICI said.
ICI said it expected the decorative paints market to grow at 1.5 times the annual growth rate of India's gross domestic product.
ICI will also manufacture automotive paints at its Chandigarh plant.

ICI's India investment is its latest expansion plan in the Asia Pacific region. The group recently opened a 15 million stg joint venture coatings plant in Guangzhou in southern China and another 15-million stg plant in Nilai, near Kuala Lumpur in Malaysia.
ICI is also building a new 25 million stg facility in Shanghai which is scheduled for completion this year.
It has also completed some acquisitions in Vietnam, the Phillippines and New Zealand.
